wtv-scramble — render pipeline benchmark

Standalone A/B/C benchmark of the Block Permute render path: the shipped v1.2.0 pipeline (Pipeline A, many <video> reads per frame), the v1.2.1 fix (Pipeline B, one <video> read per frame via an offscreen snapshot canvas), and the v1.3.0 candidate (Pipeline C, a single-draw WebGL fragment-shader gather). Runs entirely in this tab — no server, no network, nothing to install.

What this proves

Firefox re-pays the video→canvas colorspace/decode conversion on every drawImage(video, …) call, while Chrome converts the decoded frame once and reuses it for the rest of that task. The shipped renderer draws straight from the <video> element 1 (base layer) + grid² (tiles) times per frame — 82 reads at grid 9 — so its cost scales with grid² against the most expensive possible source. The v1.2.1 fix snapshots the video into an offscreen canvas once per frame, then sources every tile from that canvas instead — but field reports say Firefox still shows frametime lag and occasional freezes, most likely because that offscreen snapshot canvas is not in the DOM and can end up software-backed (a per-frame GPU→CPU download), and because IVS adaptive-bitrate rendition switches change videoWidth/videoHeight mid-stream, forcing a canvas backing reallocation. Pipeline C tests the fix for both: one GPU-resident video texture per frame, a render target whose size is not derived from the video's dimensions, and the entire tile permutation done in a single draw call on the GPU.

  • Pipeline A (old, v1.2.0 structure): 1× drawImage(video) full-frame base layer into an intermediate canvas, + grid²× drawImage(video, tile…) into that same canvas, + 1× final blit of that canvas onto the visible canvas.
  • Pipeline B (new, 2D fix, v1.2.1): 1× drawImage(video) into a reused offscreen snapshot canvas, + up to 2× border-strip copies from the snapshot, + grid²× tile copies from the snapshot straight onto the visible canvas. Zero further video-element reads that frame.
  • Pipeline C (new, WebGL, v1.3.0 candidate): 1× texImage2D(video) upload into a reused video texture, + 1× drawArrays covering the whole canvas. The fragment shader gathers every output tile in parallel: for output tile i it samples the scrambled video texture at tile perm[i], looked up from a small perm-lookup texture. Invert and flip stay pure CSS on the visible canvas in every pipeline — the shader only does the tile permutation.

All three pipelines use the identical permutation, identical tile geometry, and the identical synthetic source frame stream — the only variable under test is how each pipeline gets scrambled pixels onto the visible canvas. If WebGL is unavailable in this browser (or fails at runtime), Pipeline C is reported as unavailable and A/B still run normally.

Run it

Synthesizes its own animated video locally (canvas → captureStream(30)) — nothing is downloaded and nothing leaves this tab. Tests grid 9 then grid 3, each pipeline timed for 5 seconds, first 10 frames of every window discarded as warmup. Takes about 30 seconds total (3 pipelines × 2 grids × 5s).

Pipeline A — old (video-sourced tiles)
Intermediate work canvas, full-frame base + tiles, then blitted to this visible canvas.
Pipeline B — new (canvas-sourced tiles)
One video snapshot per frame; border strips + tiles drawn straight onto this visible canvas.
Pipeline C — WebGL (new)
One video-texture upload per frame; single draw call gathers every tile via the permutation shader. Render target size is fixed, not re-derived from the video each frame.
